subject: Request: Onramp rebate & pilot acceleration for Mediscope — VP/CFO approval needed
messages:
From: Elena Suarez <elena@mediscope.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@mediscope.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — ask on rebate and accelerated ramp

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers and the op controls. We have one practical blocker on our side that I wanted to surface quickly: our security and procurement teams need a short-term financial guardrail to cover unexpected consumption during the migration window.

Specifically, Mediscope is proposing a three-month onramp rebate that would act as a burn-safeguard while we move production traffic. The ask is: 1) a rebate covering overage consumption up to $60k for the first 90 days, and 2) an option to convert a portion of that rebate to committed spend if we hit the usage thresholds.

I realize this is outside standard pilot credits. We see material upside — if we can get a temporary cap, we can accelerate the cutover and expand to two additional product teams within Q3. Attached a short usage snapshot and SOW draft.

Can your finance/leadership team advise if Redwood can sign off on a bridged rebate with the following guardrails?
- $60k overage cap, one-time credit applied monthly
- Rebate converts to committed credit only if 3-month average usage > 500k tokens/day
- Standard security/data residency terms to remain intact

Happy to jump on a call if useful.

Best,
Elena Suarez
Head of Platform Operations
Mediscope

---
Attachment: Mediscope_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: mediscope_q1_usage_snapshot.csv (text/csv)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Redwood pilot — ask on rebate and accelerated ramp

Kimberly / Laura — forwarding Mediscope's formal ask. Quick summary and my read:

Summary:
- External asks for a 3-month onramp rebate / overage cap up to $60k to cover migration spikes.
- They want a conversion path where some or all rebate becomes committed spend if average usage exceeds threshold.
- They project significant expansion (two additional teams) if migration goes well.

Why this matters:
- High expansion potential in healthcare vertical; Mediscope is a well-funded Series C with strong product-market fit.
- Risk: short-term revenue dilution vs. long-term committed ARR.

Proposal (what I'm asking you to OK):
- Approve a time-bound rebate: max $60k credit, applied monthly over the first 3 months.
- Conversion trigger: 90-day rolling average > 500k tokens/day converts up to 50% of used rebate into committed credit at a 12-month minimum contract.
- Limitations: one rebate per customer, non-transferable, rev rec to be handled per finance guidance.

Financial ask: need VP/CFO approval for the rebate authority and for the conversion mechanics. Laura, can you run a contribution-margin impact quickly? If we expect >30% of the pilot to convert to a multi-year commitment, this seems economically reasonable.

I can draft an exec memo/one-pager for sign-off once you confirm the guardrails are acceptable. If you'd prefer, we can shorten the cap or require a smaller conversion to reduce risk.

Thanks — happy to discuss.

-MK
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Forwarded attachments: Mediscope_SOW_v1.pdf, mediscope_q1_usage_snapshot.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Redwood pilot — ask on rebate and accelerated ramp

Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks for the context. I ran a preliminary back-of-envelope on the proposed structure. Key notes:

- If we assume full $60k utilization across three months, the gross revenue at risk is $60k but the protective value is the acceleration and potential ARR.
- Contribution margin impact: with typical pilot-to-paid conversion of 35% for similar accounts we reviewed, expected payback is within 6–9 months post-conversion. I need more precise usage curves to model worst-case.

Two items I need before I can endorse a VP/CFO sign-off memo:
1) A clear conversion mechanism: what does "convert to committed credit" mean operationally? (e.g., credit applied to future invoices over 12 months vs. one-time refund). We should prefer future invoice credits tied to a signed 12-month commitment.
2) A hard cap and clawback: define a cap per month and a clawback clause if the contract is terminated within 12 months. This reduces risk for Finance.

Suggested redlines to present:
- Rebate cap: $60k total; monthly cap of $25k during months 1–3 (so they can't use all $60k in month 1).
- Conversion: up to 50% of used rebate can be applied as committed invoice credit after they sign a 12-month minimum with net 30; the remaining is non-convertible credit.
- Clawback: if they terminate within 12 months the converted portion is repayable on a pro rata basis.

If Kimberly is OK with the business case, I'll draft the memo for VP/CFO approval including a short financial table. Markus — please provide an estimated token ramp (weekly) for the pilot so I can stress-test the exposure.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal_onramp_rebate.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 15:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Redwood pilot — ask on rebate and accelerated ramp

Kimberly / Laura — thanks, Laura, this is helpful.

I talked to the Mediscope CTO this morning and pushed for a more granular ramp forecast; they sent a week-by-week estimate attached. My answers to Laura's items below:

- Conversion mechanics: Mediscope prefers credit applied to future invoices over a 12-month period (they want predictability on their ledger). We're proposing Redwood will allow converting up to 50% of used rebate into invoice credit post-signature of a 12-month minimum contract.
- Cap enforcement: Accept Laura's monthly cap of $25k for months 1–3; total not to exceed $60k.
- Clawback: Mediscope accepts a pro rata repay if contract terminated within 12 months.

Ask for Kimberly: can you sign off on granting limited commercial authority for this one-off structure (time-bound rebate + conversion path + clawback)? If yes, I'll package a one-page memo for VP/CFO (copying legal for final T&Cs).

If helpful, proposal summary for memo:
- Structure: 3-month onramp rebate, $60k total cap, $25k monthly cap
- Conversion: up to 50% of rebate convertible to invoice credit upon signing 12-month commitment
- Guardrails: clawback on early termination; one-time exception; non-transferable
- Expected outcome: accelerate cutover, 2 additional product teams in Q3, projected ARR of $420k within 12 months if conversion targets met

I'll wait for your signoff or suggestions and will get legal looped for contract language.

Thanks,
-MK
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Cc: legal@redwood.com
